coaching.title: Hills: 7 mi + 1,500 ft — Descending Focus
coaching.message: Calendar says vert day, so we run — this is Week 3 peak, not taper yet. First-light start: 7 miles with ~1,500 ft climbing. Climb steady at Zone 2 to low Zone 3 (~135-155 bpm), power hike anything steep — walking uphill fast is a skill, not a failure. The real work today is the descents: run them controlled and relaxed, quick light feet, let quads absorb the load. Julian Alps demands 8,850 ft of descent, so every downhill now is race-specific eccentric strength banking. Effort over pace on the Vegas terrain and heat.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short-but-vertful session. 30-60 min out, take ~30-40g easy carbs (banana, toast + honey, or a gel) so you climb fueled. On a 7-miler you may not need much mid-run, but rehearse race habits: sip 40-60g carbs/hr if you're out over an hour. Sodium is the headline today — 600-800 mg/hr in Vegas heat to hold hydration. Refuel within 30 min of finishing: 20-30g protein + carbs to jump-start quad repair from the descending load.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Downhill running trashes quads with micro-damage — respect it. Post-run: 5-10 min easy walk to flush, then foam roll quads, calves and glutes. Legs up the wall for 10 min. You have a gym block this evening (knee work) — keep it light and rehab-focused, no heavy loading on already-fatigued quads. Prioritize protein at dinner and aim for 8 hours of sleep; adaptation from the climb happens tonight, not on the trail.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Five weeks out and you're threading real vert around travel, a show week, and a demanding schedule — that consistency is exactly what shows up on race day. Use today's descents as rehearsal: practice the calm, quiet-footed downhill mindset you'll want when you're 8,000 ft into the Julian Alps with tired legs. Control the descent, control the race. Bank the discipline now.
